clippings.speaker: Gerard Butler
clippings.quote: I always felt like I was in more than capable hands with really a visionary genius.
clippings.title: Dean DeBlois & Gerard Butler on How to Train Your Dragon and Sequel
clippings.context: Butler reflecting on working with DeBlois on the live-action remake, in a making-of interview with Drew Taylor.

clippings.speaker: Gerard Butler
clippings.quote: …I want to thank Dean, cause he put at the very end of the movie a dedication to my mom.
clippings.title: HOW TO TRAIN YOUR DRAGON – Gerard Butler & Dean DeBlois Interview
clippings.context: Butler talking about how his mother's illness shaped his Stoick, and DeBlois's closing dedication to her, in a joint interview with DeBlois.

clippings.speaker: Gerard Butler
clippings.quote: I feel like Dean has allowed me to bring this BIG energy.
clippings.title: HOW TO TRAIN YOUR DRAGON – Gerard Butler & Dean DeBlois Interview
clippings.context: Butler on returning to voice-to-live-action Stoick, in a joint interview with DeBlois.

clippings.speaker: Dean DeBlois
clippings.quote: I think when he was able to step into those boots for real and have that 90 pound costume put on—the five pieces of his beard and wig, which he complained about all the time—he is that character.
clippings.title: The Director of 'How to Train Your Dragon' Talks Beefing Up Gerard Butler's Arc
clippings.context: DeBlois explaining, in an io9 interview by Sabina Graves, how the heavy live-action costume helped Butler become Stoick.

clippings.speaker: Dean DeBlois
clippings.quote: So we would get Gerard Butler miked across from Jay Baruchel, or Jay with Craig Ferguson, or all three of them doing a scene together, and it had kind of a natural timing, and it felt real.
clippings.title: Interview: Dean DeBlois, director of 'How To Train Your Dragon'
clippings.context: DeBlois on how the animated film's voice cast was recorded in the same room so scenes could develop between the actors.

clippings.speaker: Dean DeBlois
clippings.quote: She always imagined Stoick to have a thick Scottish brogue. So when we cast Gerard Butler, it set a standard for the adults.
clippings.title: The Way of the Dragons: Dean DeBlois on HTTYD2
clippings.context: DeBlois explaining, on the sequel's press tour, how Cressida Cowell's Scottish-accented Stoick led to Butler's casting and the accents for the adults.

notes: Butler's 2014 and 2010 interview comments about DeBlois were not found; the 2010 MovieMom quotes are from Chris Sanders, so they were skipped. An AU Review (Peter Gray) answer by DeBlois on Butler's casting is usable but its key line has a typo on the page, so it was left out.
